result.reviewScopeSummary: Reviewed Story 7 against AC-7.1 through AC-7.4, focusing on fixture creation from managed threads and PI sessions, fixture persistence shape, repair/import metadata, and the `/lh-fixture` and `/lh-status` command surfaces. I also audited the touched runtime paths in `pi-extension.ts` for real-session production behavior and ran the story and epic gates.

newFindings.title: PI runtime capture can mix two sessions into one managed thread
newFindings.evidence: `registerContextStewardExtension()` keeps one module-local `activeThread`, and `ensureActiveThread()` returns it for every later event without checking the current PI target (`src/context-steward/pi/pi-extension.ts:538-560`). Ad-hoc repro: after firing `message_end` once in `session-1` and once in `session-2` under the same cwd, the store contained only one thread directory and that thread's messages carried session ids `["session-1","session-2"]`, proving cross-session activity was appended into the first thread.

newFindings.title: `/lh-fixture pi-session` drops active-branch context and fails on branched live sessions
newFindings.evidence: `executeFixtureCommand()` builds the `pi_session` source with only `sessionFilePath` and `sessionId` (`src/context-steward/pi/pi-extension.ts:416-437`), even though `createRealSessionFixture` accepts `activeLeafId` and `sessionManager` (`src/context-steward/services/fixture-service.ts:13-21,150-170`) and `readPiActivePath()` uses those fields to disambiguate branched sessions (`src/context-steward/pi/pi-session-importer.ts:122-159`). Ad-hoc repro on a branched session with `ctx.sessionManager.getLeafId()` set to the active leaf: `executeFixtureCommand({ args: "pi-session" })` returned `FIXTURE_CREATE_FAILED` plus `IMPORT_PATH_AMBIGUOUS`, while a direct `createRealSessionFixture({... activeLeafId, sessionManager })` call succeeded.

newFindings.title: PI-session fixtures persist the session file directory instead of the real session cwd
newFindings.evidence: `loadPiSessionSnapshot()` seeds imports with `cwd: dirname(input.source.sessionFilePath)` (`src/context-steward/services/fixture-service.ts:159-166`), and `attachExistingPiSession()` writes that value into the imported thread target/runtime context (`src/context-steward/services/import-service.ts:112-130,276-281`). Ad-hoc repro wrote a session whose header `cwd` was `/tmp/.../project` and whose file lived under `/tmp/.../pi-sessions`; the resulting fixture `thread.json` persisted `target.cwd=/tmp/.../pi-sessions` instead of the session cwd, so the fixture is not a faithful thread-shaped copy of the source session metadata.

productionPathFindings: `src/context-steward/pi/pi-extension.ts` reuses one cached `activeThread` across all PI session contexts, so live runtime capture can append session B activity into session A's managed thread.

`src/context-steward/pi/pi-extension.ts` does not forward active-branch context into `/lh-fixture pi-session`, so branched current sessions can fail fixture creation even when PI exposes the active leaf.
`src/context-steward/services/fixture-service.ts` seeds PI-session imports with `dirname(sessionFilePath)` as cwd, so imported fixture thread metadata can drift from the real session cwd.
additionalObservations: No fake adapter or test-only shim was found in the PI-session fixture path itself; `createRealSessionFixture` reuses `attachExistingPiSession` against a temporary real `FileThreadStore` (`src/context-steward/services/fixture-service.ts:155-177`).
`npm run verify-all` exited 0 but currently reports `No integration tests found.`, so the epic gate is passing without the integration coverage described in the test plan.

`tests/context-steward/pi-extension-commands.test.ts` covers managed-thread fixture output and `/lh-status`, but it does not exercise `/lh-fixture pi-session` on a branched session or assert imported fixture target cwd fidelity.
